title: Surface incident action items as verifiable shipping criteria for runtime degradations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
During a recent KV-cache stall incident (postmortem link below) several operational gaps were identified: unclear PRD acceptance criteria for degraded-path mitigations, missing canary verification for automatic fallback rules, and insufficient runbook-to-PRD traceability.

Goal:
Translate prioritized postmortem actions into concrete PRD updates and verifiable shipping criteria so that product and engineering can sign off on releases that change runtime fallback behavior or rollout contracts.

Scope:
- Update the core runtime PRD to include incident-driven acceptance criteria for degradations, fallback rules, and rollback triggers.
- Add a lightweight verification harness (synthetic traffic + smoke checks) that product/infra can run as part of release sign-off for runtime-degradation changes.
- Ensure runbook steps map to PRD acceptance criteria and add explicit operator verification tasks.

Out of scope:
- Large-scale autoscaler redesign (will be tracked as a separate project).

Why this matters:
Customers observed opaque degradation behavior and long remediation loops. By encoding postmortem actions into shipping criteria we reduce blast radius of rollout changes and provide engineering with a clear verification checklist that aligns with SRE runbooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PRD change - The runtime PRD contains a dedicated section 'Degradation & Fallback Acceptance' covering at minimum: specific SLO triggers, rollback gates, canary traffic thresholds, and operator verification steps (example entries included).
2) Verification harness - A documented and runnable harness exists (CI job or one-click script) that can replay a synthetic degradation scenario and assert that fallback and rollback actions occur within defined thresholds.
3) Runbook mapping - Every runbook step referenced in the postmortem is mapped to a PRD acceptance item and has an owner.
4) Sign-off - Product, SRE, and the Runtime tech lead have recorded approval on the PRD changes and verification harness (PR or Confluence sign-off link).
5) Test coverage - New unit/integration tests or chaos checks have been added to cover the primary degraded-path flow.
6) Observability - Dashboards/datasets required to validate acceptance criteria are documented and accessible to reviewers (links in references).
decisions:
- Prioritization: We will treat degraded-path acceptance as a release blocker for any runtime change that alters fallback behavior.
- Verification approach: Lightweight synthetic harness (replay of representative KV-cache stall + canary traffic) rather than full chaos campaign for initial rollout.
- Ownership: Product owns PRD text; SRE/Runtime owns harness implementation; Engineering owns tests and instrumentation.
- Rollback criteria: If canary error rate > 2.5x baseline for 5 minutes or tail latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive windows, auto-fallback must trigger and release is blocked until investigation.
risks:
- Overly prescriptive acceptance criteria could slow shipping; we'll iterate with timeboxed guardrails.
- Synthetic harness may not cover every real-world failure mode; follow-up will expand coverage based on incident taxonomy.
- Alignment risk between on-call operators and release engineers on verification ownership.
